name: google_trends_consumption_prediction
what_it_holds: Research repo (40 stars, updated Jul 2025) comparing a Kernel-PCA Google Trends consumption indicator against the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index and the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index as predictors of US real PCE. No raw survey series committed as files, but the code pulls/uses UMich CSI and Conference Board CCI series and documents the construction and an in-sample/out-of-sample nowcasting comparison methodology (kernel PCA on Google Trends categories vs. survey indices, AR baseline).
why_useful: Gap 17 (nowcasting methods, anchored/constructed Google Trends). We already found raw Google Trends fails naive tests (0/162) on our own construction; this repo's kernel-PCA re-weighting of a consumption-relevant Trends basket, benchmarked explicitly against UMich/Conference Board, is a different construction worth stealing the method from rather than the conclusion. Low direct data value (no files), moderate method value.
time_coverage: not stated in repo card; consumption/CCI/CSI history depends on FRED vintage used
size_hint: code repo, no large data files
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold UMich/Conference Board via general macro sources and have tested raw Google Trends (failed); this is a re-weighted Trends construction, not a duplicate of the failed test.
themes: Consumer sentiment and surveys: UMich, Conference Board, NY Fed SCE, EU consumer confidence, travel-intent surveys (Longwoods, Destination Analysts, MMGY) scraped
Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos

name: remittance-update
what_it_holds: Reconstructed World Bank/KNOMAD bilateral remittance matrix extended through 2025 (KNOMAD's official matrix stops at 2021). data/output/ has bilateral_matrix_2000_2025.parquet + .csv (corridor-level flows, country pairs), country_received_2000_2025.csv, country_sent_2000_2025.csv, yearly_summary_2000_2025.csv, plus a validation comparison to the official 2021 matrix (0.963 correlation, recovers 93.3% of total flows). Built from UN DESA International Migrant Stock (2020/2024 revisions) + World Bank WDI GNI-per-capita and remittance inflow/outflow totals via WDI API; gaps filled by interpolation/extrapolation capped at +/-20% CAGR, normalized to reported country totals. ~9.3K bilateral cells in 2024 vs ~12.3K earlier years (fewer migrant-stock pairs in later years). Updated 15 days ago (active). Global country coverage, annual 2000-2025.
why_useful: Fills numbered gap #6 (consumer spend / cross-border capacity proxy): remittance flows are a standard proxy for diaspora travel and cross-border consumer strength, and this is a maintained, methodologically transparent, point-in-time-labeled (annual vintage) global bilateral series extending past the official KNOMAD 2021 cutoff into 2025 — useful as a regional (LatAm/APAC/EMEA) demand-strength cross-check for ABNB's regional nights/ADR splits.
